q: 1. According to NS, in 1 cu. m. brick masonry, number of bricks required is
explain: As per standard practice for modular bricks, about 560 bricks are needed per cubic meter of masonry.

q: 2. Sewer pipes are made of
explain: Stoneware is dense, vitrified, and chemically resistant, ideal for carrying sewage.

q: 3. Glazing of clay products, is done
options: to protect them from atmospheric effect
to protect them from corrosive action
explain: Glazing gives an impervious, attractive coating that protects clay products from weathering and corrosion.

q: 4. Formation of whitish deposit on the bricks due to the presence of excess salts is called
explain: Efflorescence is the whitish deposit of soluble salts that migrate to the brick surface and crystallize as moisture evaporates.

q: 5. The nature of ceramic material is
explain: Ceramics are characterized by high hardness and high resistance to heat, but they lack ductility and fail suddenly (brittle).

q: 6. Refractory bricks are specially manufactured
options: to have high insulation against sound
explain: Refractory bricks, also known as fire bricks, are designed to resist high temperatures (up to 1700°C) without melting or softening.

q: 7. The soil good for making bricks is
explain: Clayey soil is ideal because it provides the necessary plasticity for molding and strength after burning.

q: 8. The maximum percentage of ingredients in brick formation is
explain: Silica (sand) constitutes the largest portion of brick earth, typically ranging from 50% to 60%.

q: 9. Swelling of bricks is known as
explain: Bloating refers to the swelling/blistering of bricks, often caused by overburning or gas formation during firing.

q: 10. The percentage of alumina in good brick earth lies between
explain: Alumina is responsible for plasticity and should be between 20-30% of the brick earth volume.

q: 11. Excess of silica in brick earth causes
explain: While silica is vital, an excess makes the brick brittle and weak because it destroys the cohesion between soil particles.

q: 12. Excess of iron oxide in brick earth causes
options: the colour change i.e. from red to dark blue
explain: While iron oxide provides the red color, an excess amount during burning causes the brick to turn dark blue or blackish.

q: 13. The crushing strength of 1st class brick should not be less than
explain: 1st class bricks are required to have a minimum compressive (crushing) strength of 10.5 N/mm² or 105 kg/cm².

q: 14. For one cubic meter of brick masonry, the number of machine made brick required as per NS is
explain: According to Nepal Standards, approximately 530 machine-made bricks are required to complete 1 cubic meter of masonry.

q: 15. The number of standard bricks required for one cubic meter of brick masonry (IS standard) is
explain: For standard modular bricks (19cm x 9cm x 9cm), the nominal requirement including mortar is 500 bricks per cubic meter.

q: 16. Tiles are used for
explain: Clay tiles are versatile components used for roofing, flooring, and constructing drainage conduits.

q: 17. The amount of local brick required for one m3 masonry (As per NS norms)
explain: Due to size variations in local traditional bricks in Nepal, the norm usually estimates 560 bricks per cubic meter.

q: 18. The internal size of mould used in brick preparation is
options: smaller than the size of fully burnt brick
larger than the size of fully burnt brick
equal to the size of fully burnt brick
explain: Moulds are made 8-10% larger than the desired brick size to account for the shrinkage that occurs during drying and burning.

q: 19. The density of common bricks varies from
explain: Common clay bricks typically have a density ranging from about 1600 to 1920 kg/m3.

q: 20. Pug mill is used for
explain: A pug mill is used for 'pugging,' which is the process of kneading the clay to make it uniform and plastic for moulding.

q: 21. Percentage to silica in a good brick earth lies between
explain: Good brick earth typically contains about 50-60% silica, providing the main structural bulk of the clay.

q: 22. Which brick is adopted well ?
explain: A high-quality brick must possess all these physical characteristics: high strength, proper burning, and low porosity.

q: 23. The bricks used for lining of furnaces are
explain: Refractory bricks, made to withstand very high temperatures, are used to line furnaces.

q: 24. Terracotta is used in building for
explain: Terracotta is a glazed or unglazed fired clay used primarily for decorative architectural elements and ornamental work.

q: 25. The quantity of sand in brick is about
explain: Silica (sand) typically makes up about 50-60% of brick earth, which is roughly equivalent to 3/5ths.

q: 26. Normally the bricks (1st class) obtained from pazawah is about
explain: Pazawah (clamp) burning is less efficient than kiln burning, typically yielding about 60% good quality bricks.

q: 27. Terracotta, in building, is used for
explain: Terracotta, a fired clay product, is commonly used for decorative and ornamental architectural work.

q: 28. Lamination of bricks is caused due to
options: entrapped air in the voids of the clay
entrapped water in the voids of the clay
explain: Lamination occurs when air is trapped within the clay during machine moulding, creating thin layers or planes of weakness.

q: 29. Strike is used to remove the
explain: A strike is a wooden or metal straight-edge used to scrape off excess clay from the top of the mould.

q: 30. The strength of a brick decreases by about ........ percent when soaked in water
explain: Water absorption weakens the internal bond structure of a brick, reducing its strength by about 25% when soaked.

q: 31. The most important tool in brick laying for lifting and spreading mortar and for forming joints is
explain: The trowel is the primary hand tool used by masons to lift, spread mortar, and finish joints.

q: 32. The minimum compressive strength of first class bricks should be
explain: First class bricks are required to have a minimum compressive strength of about 10 N/mm2 as per this reference.

q: 33. The good clay for making brick is
explain: Weathering breaks down the clay particles and removes impurities, making the clay more plastic and suitable for brick molding.
